meta.name: Thai Tea Boba
meta.description: A from-scratch Thai iced tea with chewy boba, built from a 16-source synthesis. ChaTraMue tea mix brewed strong, strained twice, and chilled, then layered over warm sugar-coated tapioca pearls with a condensed-and-evaporated milk blend poured over a spoon for the signature ombré effect. Hot variation notes included inline.

change_log.summary: Initial recipe synthesized from 16-source research across food blogs, professional boba chains, and tea specialists

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.sourcedFrom: All 16 sources — standard water ratios for strong brew and 5:1+ boba cooking
ingredients.rationale: 3 cups for tea (strong concentrate that holds up to ice dilution). 4 cups for boba (rolling boil with room to move). 1 Tbsp for syrup.

ingredients.name: ChaTraMue Thai Tea Mix
ingredients.sourcedFrom: S10 (Sharetea), S5 (Carmyy), S1 (The Forked Spoon) — 11/16 sources use pre-made mix
ingredients.rationale: Pre-made mix (ChaTraMue or Pantai) is the most reliable path to authentic color and flavor. ChaTraMue (Number One Brand) is the Thai industry standard. 1/2 cup loose mix weighs approximately 40g.

ingredients.name: Dark Brown Sugar
ingredients.sourcedFrom: S4 (Oh, How Civilized), S5 (Carmyy), S9 (Mountain Rose Herbs) — brown sugar preferred over white for depth
ingredients.rationale: Brown sugar adds molasses depth that complements the tea's malty character. Split between tea brewing and boba syrup coating.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.sourcedFrom: S6 (Simply Suwanee) — 1/8 tsp salt in tea base
ingredients.rationale: A pinch of salt rounds out the tea's bitterness and enhances sweetness perception. Standard Thai tea shop technique.

ingredients.name: Quick-Cook Tapioca Pearls
ingredients.sourcedFrom: S1 (The Forked Spoon), S10 (Sharetea) — 10/16 sources use quick-cook; WuFuYuan brand recommended
ingredients.rationale: Quick-cook pearls (5-7 min) deliver excellent texture with minimal effort. 1/2 cup dry pearls weighs approximately 80g, yielding enough for 2 generous servings.

ingredients.name: Sweetened Condensed Milk
ingredients.sourcedFrom: S4 (Oh, How Civilized), S6 (Simply Suwanee), S7 (Honest Food Talks) — 9/16 sources use condensed + evaporated combo
ingredients.rationale: The condensed + evaporated combination is the strongest consensus across sources (9/16). Condensed provides sweetness and body. 3 Tbsp = approximately 60g (dense liquid).

ingredients.name: Evaporated Milk
ingredients.sourcedFrom: S4 (Oh, How Civilized), S6 (Simply Suwanee), S7 (Honest Food Talks) — evaporated adds creaminess without excessive sweetness
ingredients.rationale: Evaporated milk adds dairy richness and creaminess without the cloying sweetness of using condensed milk alone. 3 Tbsp = approximately 45g.

ingredients.name: Ice
ingredients.sourcedFrom: All 16 sources — standard iced tea service
ingredients.rationale: Approximately 1 cup per glass. Tea is brewed as a concentrate specifically to withstand ice dilution.

states.title: Boil Water for Tea
states.direction: In medium saucepan (V1), bring 711g water to a rolling boil — 212°F (100°C) — over high heat.
states.exit_condition: Water is at a full rolling boil — 212°F (100°C)

states.title: Add Tea Mix and Sugar
states.direction: Remove from heat. Add 40g ChaTraMue Thai tea mix and 26g brown sugar. Stir to combine, then return to low heat.
states.exit_condition: Tea mix and sugar are stirred into the hot water, sugar dissolving

notes.text: For a hot variation: use only 474g water (2 cups) instead of 711g for a more concentrated brew that won't be diluted by ice
For a hot variation: optionally add 1 star anise pod here for a warm spice note during steeping

states.title: Simmer Covered
states.direction: Cover the saucepan and simmer on low heat for 3 minutes. Do not boil — a gentle simmer extracts flavor without excessive bitterness.
states.exit_condition: 3 minutes elapsed, tea is deeply colored and aromatic

notes.text: Keep the lid on — the steam helps extract more flavor from the tea mix

states.title: Steep Off Heat
states.direction: Remove from heat, keep covered, and steep for 15-20 minutes. The tea will continue to darken and develop its characteristic deep orange-amber color.
states.exit_condition: 15-20 minutes elapsed, tea is very dark and intensely aromatic

notes.text: Longer steeping (up to 20 min) produces a stronger, more robust tea that stands up better to ice and milk dilution
Start the boba syrup and boba cooking during this steeping time to work in parallel

states.title: Strain Tea Twice
states.direction: Set fine-mesh strainer (V4) over heat-proof pitcher (V2). Pour tea through strainer. Discard leaves, rinse strainer, and strain a second time for a cleaner, sediment-free concentrate.
states.exit_condition: Tea is strained twice into pitcher, no visible sediment or leaf particles

notes.text: The double strain is what separates good Thai tea from gritty Thai tea — the mix is very fine and passes through a single strain
If you have cheesecloth, line the strainer on the second pass for even cleaner results

states.title: Add Salt to Tea
states.direction: Stir 1g salt into the strained tea concentrate. The salt rounds out bitterness and enhances the perception of sweetness.
states.exit_condition: Salt fully dissolved into the tea concentrate

states.title: Chill Tea Concentrate
states.direction: Refrigerate the tea concentrate for at least 30 minutes, or until cold. For faster chilling, set the pitcher in an ice bath.
states.exit_condition: Tea concentrate is cold to the touch

notes.text: The tea must be cold before assembly — warm tea melts the ice too fast and dilutes the drink
For a hot variation: skip this step entirely. Keep the tea warm.

states.title: Make Brown Sugar Syrup
states.direction: In small saucepan (V3), combine 26g dark brown sugar and 15g water. Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, until sugar dissolves and mixture thickens into a syrup, about 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
states.exit_condition: Sugar fully dissolved, mixture is a thick, glossy brown syrup

notes.text: The syrup should coat the back of a spoon but still be pourable — not caramelized to hard crack
Try: muscovado sugar for even deeper molasses flavor (Carmyy approach)

states.title: Boil Water for Boba
states.direction: In medium saucepan (V1, rinsed from tea), bring 948g water to a vigorous rolling boil — 212°F (100°C) — over high heat. The water must be at a full boil before adding pearls.
states.exit_condition: Water is at a vigorous rolling boil — 212°F (100°C)

notes.text: The 5:1+ water-to-pearl ratio is critical — pearls need room to tumble freely without sticking together

states.title: Cook Tapioca Pearls
states.direction: Add 80g tapioca pearls to the boiling water. Stir immediately to prevent sticking. Cook at a rolling boil for 5-7 minutes, stirring every 1-2 minutes, until pearls are uniformly translucent with no white center.
states.exit_condition: Pearls are uniformly translucent throughout — no opaque white centers visible when held up to light

notes.text: Stir immediately after adding to prevent pearls from sinking and fusing to the bottom of the pot
Test a pearl by biting it in half — it should be uniformly translucent and chewy throughout with no hard white core

states.title: Drain and Toss in Syrup
states.direction: Drain cooked pearls through fine-mesh strainer (V4). Immediately transfer hot pearls to the small saucepan (V3) with the brown sugar syrup. Toss gently to coat every pearl.
states.exit_condition: All pearls are evenly coated in brown sugar syrup, glossy and warm

notes.text: Boba must be served within 2 hours of cooking — they harden irreversibly as they cool. This is the single most important timing constraint in the entire recipe.
Keep the syrup-coated boba warm until assembly. The syrup prevents sticking and adds sweetness.

states.title: Mix Milk Blend
states.direction: In small bowl (V5), combine 60g sweetened condensed milk and 45g evaporated milk. Stir until smooth and uniform.
states.exit_condition: Milk mixture is smooth and homogeneous, no streaks of condensed milk visible

notes.text: The condensed + evaporated combination is the strongest consensus across sources (9/16) — it delivers authentic Thai tea shop creaminess
For a hot variation: warm the milk mixture gently before adding to tea, and increase evaporated to 60g (4 Tbsp) for a latte-like body

states.title: Build the Drink
states.direction: For each glass: spoon warm boba into the bottom. Fill glass with 140g ice. Pour chilled tea concentrate to three-quarters full. Slowly pour half the milk mixture over the back of a spoon held just above the surface to create an ombré layer effect. Serve with a wide boba straw.
states.exit_condition: Two glasses assembled with visible layers: boba on bottom, dark tea in middle, creamy milk floating on top

notes.text: The ombré effect is purely visual — the drinker stirs before drinking. But it makes for a beautiful presentation.
Use a wide boba straw (12mm+) — standard straws cannot pick up the tapioca pearls
For a hot variation: skip ice, pour warm tea to 3/4, top with warm milk mixture. Still serve boba warm on the bottom.
Consider: freeze leftover brewed tea in ice cube trays for no-dilution iced Thai tea next time

research.strategy: 16 parallel source analysis covering food blogs, professional boba chains, restaurateur recipes, tea specialists, and vegan adaptations. Cross-referenced ingredient ratios, milk combinations, tea brands, and boba cooking techniques to build consensus-driven master recipe.

techniques.name: Double strain for sediment-free tea
techniques.rationale: ChaTraMue mix contains very fine particles that pass through a single strain. Double straining produces a cleaner, smoother concentrate without gritty sediment.

techniques.name: Condensed + evaporated milk combination
techniques.sourcedFrom: S4 (Oh, How Civilized), S6 (Simply Suwanee), S7 (Honest Food Talks), S10 (Sharetea)
techniques.rationale: 9/16 sources use this combination. Condensed provides sweetness and body; evaporated adds dairy richness without cloying sweetness. This is the authentic Thai tea shop approach.

techniques.name: Brown sugar boba syrup coating
techniques.sourcedFrom: S5 (Carmyy), S11 (Teak & Thyme), S14 (Pick Up Limes)
techniques.rationale: Tossing freshly drained pearls in brown sugar syrup prevents sticking, adds sweetness, and keeps pearls warm. Brown sugar adds molasses depth over white sugar.

techniques.name: 5:1+ water ratio for boba cooking
techniques.rationale: Pearls need ample room to tumble freely in vigorously boiling water. Insufficient water causes clumping and uneven cooking.

techniques.name: Serve boba within 2 hours
techniques.rationale: Tapioca pearls undergo retrogradation as they cool — starch molecules re-crystallize, creating an irreversibly hard texture. No reheating method fully restores freshly-cooked chewiness.

techniques.name: Ombré pour over spoon
techniques.sourcedFrom: S1 (The Forked Spoon), S4 (Oh, How Civilized)
techniques.rationale: Pouring milk mixture slowly over the back of a spoon creates a visible layered gradient (dark tea to creamy white). Purely visual — drinker stirs before consuming.

methods.detail: Best fresh. Boba hardens in the fridge — make only what you'll drink.
Tea concentrate keeps 2–3 days in the fridge. Pour over fresh ice and milk to serve.
